title: Regional policing unit drops controversial Palantir AI technology
key_facts: The East Midlands Special Operations Unit (EMSOU), which tackles serious and organised crime in Derbyshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, Nottinghamshire and Northamptonshire, will not continue with Palantir software after a two-year trial.
The trial began in October 2024 to test whether the software could help investigate crime without compromising ethics.
EMSOU decided not to fund a new contract and says Palantir must show it has cut links with the force's systems and deleted all its data.
The trial fed data from Leicestershire Police into Palantir's Foundry operating system, which uses AI and machine learning.
Regional Assistant Chief Constable Ian Green said the decision followed scoping work and an assessment of what it would deliver, including future funding, after Home Office funding ended.
EMSOU would not say how Palantir was used, which datasets were used (operational security) or what it cost (commercial confidentiality).
Palantir says its software is used by 11 UK police forces, the NHS and the Ministry of Defence and gave examples of crime-fighting results.
Amnesty International UK welcomed the decision; critics also raise Palantir's role in Israel's use in Gaza, US immigration enforcement and the US military's Maven system.
